\section[\ar{أخضر}, \ar{أصفر}]{\ar{أخضر}, \ar{أصفر} — "greens" you'd recognize, and a hidden zero}

\label{lesson:AR-C22-akhdar-asfar}



\begin{quote}
\textbf{Warm-up.} {[}PAUSE 2s{]} Arabic's green word hides an English-style pun. Its yellow word hides something even better — the exact root behind the word "zero" itself.
\end{quote}

\begin{culture}
\textbf{\ar{أخضر}} (\emph{akhḍar}, "\textbf{green}") comes from the root \textbf{\ar{خ}-\ar{ض}-\ar{ر}} (\emph{kh-ḍ-r}, "\textbf{to be green}"). That same root gives \textbf{\ar{خضار}} (\emph{khuḍār}, "\textbf{vegetables}") — echoing the exact same move English makes when it calls vegetables "\textbf{greens}." The same root also names the mysterious Quranic figure \textbf{\ar{الخِضْر}} (\emph{al-Khiḍr}), "\textbf{the Green One}" — traditionally said to be called this because the ground turned green wherever he sat or prayed.
\end{culture}

\begin{culture}
Here's the real surprise: \textbf{\ar{أصفر}} (\emph{aṣfar}, "\textbf{yellow}") shares its root, \textbf{\ar{ص}-\ar{ف}-\ar{ر}} (\emph{ṣ-f-r}), with \textbf{\ar{صفر}} (\emph{ṣifr}, "\textbf{zero, empty, void}") — the \textbf{exact} Arabic word that gave English both \textbf{zero} (via Italian \emph{zefiro}/\emph{zero}) and \textbf{cipher} (via Medieval Latin \emph{cifra}). So the same three-letter Arabic root sits behind "yellow" and behind the number \textbf{zero} itself. The sources don't fully explain \emph{why} "emptiness" and "yellow" share a root — but the shared root itself, connecting Arabic's yellow-word straight back to the origin of "zero," is genuine and well documented.
\end{culture}

\subsection*{Guided Practice}
{[}PAUSE 1s{]}

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item {[}YOU SAY: "akhḍar" — green, same root as "khuḍār," vegetables{]}
  \item {[}YOU SAY: "aṣfar" — yellow, same root as "ṣifr," zero{]}
  \item {[}YOU SAY: the connection — "aṣfar, ṣifr, zero, cipher" — one Arabic root, reaching all the way into English math vocabulary{]}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Wrap-up recall}]
{[}PAUSE 3s{]} What root does \textbf{\ar{أخضر}} share with "vegetables," and what English phrase does this echo? (\textbf{\ar{خ}-\ar{ض}-\ar{ر}}, \emph{kh-ḍ-r} — echoes English calling vegetables "\textbf{greens}.") What Quranic figure shares this root, and what does his name mean? (\textbf{\ar{الخِضْر}}, \emph{al-Khiḍr} — "\textbf{the Green One}.") What word does \textbf{\ar{أصفر}} share its root with, and what two English words trace back to it? (\textbf{\ar{صفر}}, \emph{ṣifr}, "zero, empty" — the source of English \textbf{zero} and \textbf{cipher}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
